translated_text: Ligninice, July 15, 1940. My darling love, today is a day, but I know that without a letter, but in Agde and on Thursday, you know, you needed this day to realize. I think I have your courage. My arm in my chair, I am, as in the mornings, settled in the tiny garden of our house and I wait, with Blacky at my feet, for the sun to decide. We have been in Ligninice for a month, maybe three beautiful summer days. Otherwise, everything is fine. A doctor told me it was normal and that the baby would probably come between the 25th and the 5th. I would obviously like to be near a large city to give birth. In Ussel, there is nothing; you have to go all the way to Tulle, which is 60 km away. I need a good doctor, but he doesn't have a clinic, and with him, I would have to stay at home, which I don't value. - We would need to know if maternity ward. No wish at all for that in Béziers there is Pezenas there isn't but 20 km is still okay if we have the car. The car is here; I haven't used it at all since June. I must not have a battery. Deep down, it doesn't matter. The days are very monotonous here; we do nothing but sleep, read, eat, knit and wait for the letters. I read some good books and I knitted a little for the baby; I often rested a lot, who knows, you might be able to do it later, so I tried to take advantage of it. It certainly wasn't real rest, because all the time I... I would have worries because of you, but physically it was better than nothing. How is your health and your nerves!?? Mr. Balmelle told me in one of his letters that you were wounded by a bullet. That's not scary, is it??? But I'm a little worried about you. Will things be alright on that front? We heard from Maria about her house. Her house was bombed; eight bombs fell near it. The Italians, but there was no damage. She's thankfully safe. Her husband, Dr. Brody, is in Marseille. He's a military doctor, Charles D'André Prody. We haven't heard from him since. He's either a prisoner or something. It's terrible. May 13th – I wrote to my mother, Metzl, in Paris, but I don't expect a reply right away. They are. The Lenards... I wonder where we are. Bobchen, I've never wanted to be with you so much and talk about everything. I have so much to tell you and can't do it now, it's no longer a question of "My God, where did you go from Pezenas?" He returned the Squill days, but I hope, but what things only, only! Three have arrived in the meantime, Liebchens of the days / every day, Little one, I hope you will write to me now as before, I write to you myself, I kiss you a thousand and a thousand times, holding you tight, very tight in my two arms that love you, your Baba.
